description: How a theme becomes colours in views-shell. The input is an Omarchy theme directory (colors.toml, optionally shell.toml), exactly as Omarchy reads it. This file is the binding only: which colour ids each Omarchy key sets. It holds no colour values; those come from the theme you pass (examples/themes/).

provenance.chromium: ui/color/color_id.h at df5b64d97601a26870372adb1ed6f5ad308365bd; every kColorSys id below was checked there
provenance.notes: (private scoping notes) theme-input.md section 5; reconciled with private scoping note views-first-rebalance.md (no cros.sys or kColorAsh ids: the Ash colour stack is not ported)

input.directory: An Omarchy theme directory. views-shell reads $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/views-shell/themes/<name>/ and ~/.config/omarchy/themes/<name>/ (PROPOSED, open decision P18), and stages the active one under $XDG_STATE_HOME/views-shell/current/theme.
input.colors.toml: Resolved with a port of Omarchy's cascade: color0 = background, color7 = foreground, color8 = muted, color15 = bright_foreground, bright_* derived as +20% white when absent, cursor and selection_foreground = bright_foreground. Unknown keys are kept and readable by plugins.

layer1_seed.note: The ColorProviderKey every views-shell widget is built with. It is the same seed Chrome receives through the BrowserThemeColor managed policy, so the stock roles views-shell does not pin are the tonal renditions Chrome draws its own frame with.
layer1_seed.color_mode: colors.toml mode (resolved from mode, a light.mode file, or background luminance)
layer1_seed.user_color: chromium.theme r,g,b if the theme ships one, else background, after seed neutralisation: if max+min <= 16, or max >= 250 with chroma <= 4, use the channel average
layer1_seed.user_color_source: kAccent (the branch ThemeService::GetColorProviderKey takes for a policy colour)
layer1_seed.scheme_variant: kTonalSpot (Chrome's default; no policy sets it)

layer2_pins.note: One ColorMixer appended last with ColorProviderManager::AppendColorProviderInitializer. Each id is SET to the resolved value of its Omarchy key. Ids not listed keep layer 1.

layer3_surfaces.note: Only when the theme directory has shell.toml. A section's values win over layer 2 for the views-shell surface of the same kind. Gradients collapse to their first stop (Omarchy's own flat fallback). Widths and alphas are honoured.
layer3_surfaces.[bar]: the bar layer surface: background, background-alpha, text, active
layer3_surfaces.[popups]: every bubble anchored to the bar (detail pages, OSD, dropdowns)
layer3_surfaces.[notifications]: message_center popups; countdown as a progress ring
layer3_surfaces.[launcher]: the launcher overlay card and scrim
layer3_surfaces.[controls]: state fills of stock buttons and toggles through kColorSysStateHover*/Pressed alphas
layer3_surfaces.[font] base-size: scales the views-shell TypographyProvider over views::style
layer3_surfaces.[lock]: ignored: the lock screen is not a views-shell surface (rule R4)

unmapped_by_design: blue, cyan, magenta, orange, brown and the bright_* hues: no shell chrome role; plugins may read them by name for data colours
green and yellow: ui/color has no kColorSys success or warning role at df5b64d9; status pills and plugins read them by name
gradient borders: first stop only; no fx work
extra keys a theme carries for other consumers (brand, desktop_background, inactive_border, terminal_color7, nvim_catppuccin_flavour, claude_code_theme, ...): kept, readable by plugins, never pinned
